what: M0 of docs/steps/settings-mcp-plan.md: Access managed OAuth on a path-scoped application (B) and on a Worker's own host (C), probes P1–P13 and P15 of docs/research/access-managed-oauth.md and the plan, run on a throwaway workers.dev stage

A.managedOAuth: off, except during deploy 2 (P2 as written)

deploys: 1: probe Workers, no new application (P1 baseline)
2: managed OAuth on A (P2–P5 and P6's authorize as the research file writes them)
3: A's OAuth off, path cookie on A; B and C made with managed OAuth (P2, P3, P5, P6, P8, P9, P12 stand-in)
4: twelve throwaway applications for P11; C alone also allows vscode://vscode.mcp/callback (allowlist scope)
5: P11 applications and C's extra URI removed; probe fixes (a 2025 GET stream answers 405; a cut ends the stream)

basis: P2/P9: with managed OAuth on B (or on A) Access answers none of the host's root or path-inserted RFC 8414 / RFC 9728 documents; t3's root /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server and /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource[/mcp] are still the origin's

P8: the more specific application wins: /_t3flare/mcp and /_t3flare/mcp/* are B's, /_t3flare/mcpx and every other /_t3flare path A's; cookies carry Path=/_t3flare/mcp and Path=/_t3flare and Access reads the first CF_Authorization, which a browser sends longer-path first

P6: a path-scoped resource (https://<host>/_t3flare/mcp, with or without ?elicitation_mode=…, or a trailing slash) is accepted at authorize and resolved to B (the login redirect carries B's aud); the host root and other paths are invalid_target

P12 (stand-in): an Access token (CF_Authorization JWT, as cookie, cf-access-token header or bearer) issued by B, A or C is refused at every other application's paths; the oauth: bearer itself is confirmed by owner step 1
conditions: Owner step 1 must show B's OAuth token refused at /_t3flare/echo and /_t3flare/harness (P12) and the token exchange working for the path resource (P6); if either fails, (C), which passed the same pre-sign-in probes, is the layout

Under (B) discovery depends on the client following WWW-Authenticate's resource_metadata (Access's own /.well-known/cloudflare-access-protected-resource/_t3flare/mcp); a client that ignored it would fall back to t3's root documents and t3's own authorization server. Claude Code, pi, Codex and OpenCode all followed it (m0-clients.json); Cursor is owner step 2. Under (C) Access serves the standard documents on the host
Only workers.dev was probed (P9 is therefore the whole run); prod's custom domain was not, since a second stage with a domain in the zone would take over prod's rate-limit ruleset (alchemy.run.ts)

basis: Access's 401 resource_metadata and protected-resource document ignore the query: resource is https://<host>/_t3flare/mcp
Claude Code, pi and Codex send that resource (no query) at authorize; OpenCode sends the configured URL with the query; Access accepts both at authorize and resolves both to the application
The query reaches the origin through Access (service token, B and C); a custom header X-T3flare-Elicitation-Mode also does, so the fallback stays available
OpenCode 2.2.7 appends its own codemode=false to the server URL's query: the endpoint must accept other query parameters and judge only elicitation_mode
modeCarrier.open: the token's use at the URL with the query (owner step 1, atEndpointWithQuery) and OpenCode's token exchange with a query resource (owner step 1, flow C)

basis: Claude Code 2.1.322: http://localhost:<port>/callback; pi 1.5.2: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback; Codex 0.167.2: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback/<random>; OpenCode 2.2.7: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback (all dynamic registration, captured before sign-in)

Cursor (third-party reports, not run here): current desktop releases use http://localhost:8787/callback (covered by allowAnyOnLocalhost), older ones cursor://anysphere.cursor-mcp/oauth/callback; Cursor web and Cloud Agents use https://www.cursor.com/agents/mcp/oauth/callback, which is not allowed (no https redirect, D13). A report says Cursor desktop may register the https URI while authorizing with localhost; owner step 2 settles it
Unlisted custom schemes, https and non-loopback http redirects are refused at registration with invalid_client_metadata 'redirect_uri is not allowed by the account configuration'

Registration (one team-wide endpoint, no resource) admits a redirect allowed by any of the team's applications, after up to a minute's propagation; authorize then enforces the application's own list (B refused a URI only C allowed with invalid_request)

P1.answer: Before managed OAuth: /_t3flare/mcp and /_t3flare answer 302 to the team login with a WWW-Authenticate 'Cloudflare-Access resource_metadata=…/.well-known/cloudflare-access-protected-resource/<path>' even without OAuth; Access already serves that document per path (authentication_methods: cloudflared only); t3's root AS and PRM documents (resource …/mcp, issuer the host) answer 200 from the origin; path-inserted documents 404

P2.answer: Managed OAuth on (A as the research file writes it, then B): a non-browser request gets 401 'Bearer realm="OAuth", error="invalid_token", …, resource_metadata="https://<host>/.well-known/cloudflare-access-protected-resource/<request path>"' with the same JSON body; no scope parameter. That document gains authentication_methods oauth and names resource https://<host>/<request path> (query dropped) and authorization_servers [the team domain]. The AS metadata is the team's (issuer and every endpoint on spirit-led-software.cloudflareaccess.com, registration_endpoint included, S256, grants authorization_code and refresh_token, no client_id_metadata_document_supported). Access answers none of the root or path-inserted RFC 8414/9728 documents on the t3 host; /cdn-cgi/access/certs answers on the app host, /cdn-cgi/access/oauth/authorization 400s there and registration 404s

Same on A, B and C
